digest.headline: US inflation climbed to 3.8% as Wall Street shares pared losses and the Sensex jumped 1,502 points.

lede.b: US consumer prices rose to 3.8% over the year, which means the general cost of living grew faster. Central banks use interest rates, like the price you pay to borrow money, to try and keep these price increases steady. Wall Street stocks fell at first due to worries about artificial intelligence technology, but then recovered some ground. Stock shares are tiny pieces of ownership in a company that you can buy and sell. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq indexes both finished the session lower.
lede.i: US inflation accelerated to 3.8%, exceeding the central bank target and increasing policy pressure on officials. Wall Street equities closed lower while paring steeper intraday losses from session lows. The Nasdaq 100 touched bear market territory during heavy technology liquidations before buyers returned. An equal-weight S&P 500 fund outperformed the standard index by 1.08 points.
lede.a: US inflation printed at 3.8%, widening the spread above the Federal Reserve target and compounding policy friction. Equity indices rebounded from severe intraday troughs as bargain hunters absorbed liquidation pressure in technology shares. The Nasdaq 100 briefly breached bear market parameters amid artificial intelligence sector unwinds before broader market breadth stabilized. The equal-weight S&P 500 outperformed its capitalization-weighted counterpart by 1.08 points.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: US inflation rises to 3.8% as stocks rebound

stories.t: US inflation climbs above Federal Reserve target
stories.b: The US rate of price increases, known as inflation, climbed to 3.8%. This moves further above the official target set by the Federal Reserve, which is the country's central bank that manages money and interest rates. Higher price growth makes everyday goods and services more expensive for everyone.
stories.i: US inflation climbed to 3.8%, moving further above the official Federal Reserve target. This acceleration increases pressure on central bank policymakers who use interest rates to manage price stability. Higher consumer prices erode purchasing power across the broader economy.
stories.a: US headline inflation printed at 3.8%, compounding the distance from the Federal Reserve's target rate. This upside print complicates monetary policy transmission as policymakers weigh sticky price pressures against growth indicators. Bond yields react to the persistent spread between actual price growth and the central bank's objective.

stories.t: Wall Street equities pare losses from session lows
stories.b: Wall Street indices like the S&P 500 and Nasdaq finished their trading day down overall. However, investors stepped in to buy stocks at lower prices, helping shares bounce back from much deeper losses earlier in the day. The Nasdaq 100 had previously entered bear market territory, meaning its value had fallen by 20% or more from a recent peak, driven down by anxiety over artificial intelligence.
stories.i: The S&P 500 and Nasdaq indices closed lower but pared steep intraday losses as investors bought shares at a discount. The Nasdaq 100 previously touched bear market territory amid heavy selling driven by artificial intelligence angst. Chip stocks slipped while materials advanced, and an equal-weight S&P 500 fund outperformed the standard index by 1.08 points on Wednesday.
stories.a: Major US equity benchmarks including the S&P 500 and Nasdaq recovered from session lows as dip-buyers absorbed forced liquidations. The Nasdaq 100 breached bear market thresholds during the session as sector-specific valuation concerns in artificial intelligence triggered broad de-risking. Meanwhile, breadth dynamics shifted as an equal-weight S&P 500 vehicle outperformed the market capitalisation-weighted index by 1.08 points on Wednesday amid a rotation out of semiconductors and into materials.

politics.b: A recent economic report called the Beige Book confirmed that the United States economy remains hot and wage pressures are building. Companies are paying workers more as business activity stays strong. This report gathers real-world economic conditions from across the country.
politics.i: The Federal Reserve's Beige Book confirmed a hot US economy alongside building wage pressures across regions. Business contacts reported steady activity levels and upward adjustments in employee compensation. These observations reflect localized business feedback compiled ahead of upcoming policy decisions.
politics.a: The latest Beige Book publication verified sustained economic activity paired with accelerating wage pressures across multiple Federal Reserve districts. Tight labor market dynamics continue to manifest in rising compensation demands reported by business contacts. This qualitative data feeds directly into the central bank's assessment of aggregate demand and capacity constraints.

timeline: US inflation climbed to 3.8% in the latest data release.
The Federal Reserve released its Beige Book confirming a hot economy and wage pressure.
The Nasdaq 100 entered bear market territory amid technology sector losses.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom

stories.t: Bank of England revises price growth outlook
stories.b: The Bank of England is the group that manages the money in the United Kingdom. Price growth measures how fast the cost of everyday things goes up over time. The Bank of England stated that price increases might stay lower than earlier forecasts suggested. This update changes how people think about future costs. The report came out on 25 November 2026.
stories.i: The Bank of England evaluates macro data to steer monetary policy. Inflation metrics might undershoot previous projections according to recent official statements. This adjustment alters trajectory expectations for benchmark borrowing costs. The central bank released the updated outlook on 25 November 2026.
stories.a: The Bank of England recalibrated its terminal rate expectations following soft medium-term pricing trajectories. Real yields adjusted as the implied terminal rate shifted lower on the curve. This deceleration thesis contrasts with prior hawkish persistence models. The central bank published the updated projection on 25 November 2026.

Germany.sub: German shares decline as economic growth eases

stories.t: Frankfurt equities drop
stories.b: German stocks fell at the end of the trading day. The DAX index dropped by 1.14%. Share prices moved lower as investors sold artificial intelligence stocks.
stories.i: German shares closed lower as the DAX fell 1.14%. A broad flight from artificial intelligence stocks drove the decline in Frankfurt.
stories.a: The DAX declined by 1.14% at the Frankfurt close. Broad sectoral liquidation in artificial intelligence equities drove the index lower.

stories.b: German quarterly economic growth slowed down. This indicator measures the total value of goods and services produced. The DAX index declined alongside this easing growth.
stories.i: German quarterly GDP growth eased. The DAX index declined as this economic indicator cooled.
stories.a: German quarterly GDP growth eased alongside the contraction in the DAX index. Macroeconomic output deceleration accompanied the equity sell-off.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Mitsui asset overhaul, crude shipments, and currency shifts

stories.t: Mitsui Plans Asset Overhaul
stories.b: Mitsui wants to change how its business works. The firm announced a plan worth $125bn to overhaul assets. The goal is to boost its return on equity. Return on equity is a measure of how well a company uses investments to grow profits.
stories.i: Mitsui targets a business asset overhaul valued at $125bn. The Japanese conglomerate implements this restructuring strategy to boost its return on equity. Management structures the portfolio realignment to improve capital efficiency across core divisions.
stories.a: Mitsui initiates a $125bn asset overhaul focused on return on equity expansion. The reallocation targets sub-performing units to compress capital intensity. Market participants must assess whether asset disposals dilute earnings power before realizing valuation multiples.

stories.t: Petrobras Crude Reaches Japan
stories.b: Petrobras shipped pre-salt crude to Japan for the first time. The tanker carried about 950,000 barrels from the Libra field to Idemitsu. The shipment happened because the Hormuz crisis cut Middle Eastern oil supplies.
stories.i: Petrobras completed its first shipment of pre-salt crude to Japan. The energy firm delivered roughly 950,000 barrels from the Libra field to Idemitsu. This diversion stems from Middle Eastern oil supply cuts driven by the Hormuz crisis.
stories.a: Petrobras executed a debut pre-salt crude delivery to Japan, dispatching approximately 950,000 barrels from the Libra field to Idemitsu. The transaction reflects trade flow realignments triggered by Middle Eastern supply disruptions under the Hormuz crisis.

stories.t: Currency Moves and Rice Ball Prices
stories.src: Euronext Markets · Seoul Economic Daily · WSJ
stories.b: The yen gained strength as the dollar slipped during an AI-driven market session. At the same time, convenience store rice balls in Japan neared 200 yen after an 80% jump. Bank of Japan Governor Ueda also stated he watches Federal Reserve moves closely.
stories.i: The yen rose alongside the Swiss franc as the dollar weakened in a volatile AI-driven session. Convenience store rice balls in Japan approached 200 yen following an 80% price jump. Bank of Japan Governor Ueda vowed to keep a careful eye on Federal Reserve decisions.
stories.a: The yen and the Swiss franc appreciated as the dollar retreated during volatile AI-driven trading sessions. Japanese convenience store rice balls traded near 200 yen following an 80% price surge. Bank of Japan Governor Ueda articulated continued scrutiny of Federal Reserve policy trajectories.

politics.b: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda stated he keeps a careful eye on the moves made by the Federal Reserve in the United States.
politics.i: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda vowed to monitor Federal Reserve policy developments.
politics.a: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda underscored attentiveness to Federal Reserve policy shifts.

timeline: Bank of Japan Governor Ueda vows to watch Federal Reserve moves.
Mitsui announces a $125bn asset overhaul plan.

China.label: China
China.sub: Shanghai Composite slips below 3,500 as tech leads drop

stories.t: Shanghai Composite Dips Below 3,500
stories.b: The Shanghai Composite index dropped below 3,500. Technology shares led this downward move. Total market turnover shrank to 1.39 trillion yuan.
stories.i: The Shanghai Composite breached the 3,500 threshold as technology shares drove the sell-off. Market turnover contracted to 1.39 trillion yuan during the session.
stories.a: The Shanghai Composite crossed beneath 3,500 amid broad tech-led liquidation. Liquidity contracted concurrently, with aggregate turnover printing at 1.39 trillion yuan.

stories.t: State Banks Accelerate Lending and Relending Signings
stories.b: China's three largest state banks promised to speed up their lending. Signings for stock buyback relending topped 460 billion yuan.
stories.i: China's big three state-owned lenders committed to accelerating loan disbursement speeds. Stock buyback relending agreement values surpassed 460 billion yuan.
stories.a: The primary state-owned banking trio pledged accelerated credit expansion timelines. Aggregate volume for stock buyback relending execution surpassed 460 billion yuan.

stories.t: Victory Giant Technology Issues Dividend After Share Drop
stories.b: Victory Giant Technology declared a dividend of 983 million yuan. This followed a 70% fall in the company's stock price. The controlling shareholder's fortune shrunk by over 50 billion yuan.
stories.i: Victory Giant Technology announced a 983 million yuan dividend following a 70% equity price decline. The controlling shareholder experienced a wealth reduction exceeding 50 billion yuan.
stories.a: Victory Giant Technology distributed a 983 million yuan dividend subsequent to a 70% equity retracement. The controlling shareholder's net worth compressed by more than 50 billion yuan.

politics.b: China widened an anti-graft crackdown. The sweep targeted former officials and crypto assets.
politics.i: China broadened its ongoing anti-corruption campaign. The expanded graft sweep targeted former government officials alongside digital currencies.
politics.a: Regulatory authorities widened the scope of the graft crackdown. The enforcement sweep incorporated both former officials and digital currency channels.

India.label: India
India.sub: Sensex gains 1,502 points as foreign inflows lift markets

stories.t: Sensex Jumps as Foreign Funds Flow In
stories.b: The Sensex is a big index, which is a basket of major company shares used to track the stock market. It jumped by 1,502 points on November 25, 2026. Banking and FMCG stocks led this rally. Foreign money entering the country and lower crude oil prices helped push the index up.
stories.i: The Sensex climbed 1,502 points on November 25, 2026, driven by rallies in banking and fast-moving consumer goods sectors. Strong foreign fund inflows and lower crude oil prices supported the broader market advance. Meanwhile, the Nifty 50 approached its record peak and neared the 26,000 mark.
stories.a: The Sensex advanced 1,502 points on November 25, 2026, propelled by sustained foreign portfolio inflows and cheaper crude oil. Large-cap banking and FMCG equities drove the headline index higher, while the Nifty 50 traded near the 26,000 threshold, testing overbought territory.

stories.t: RBI Plans Variable Rate Repo Auction
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India is the central bank, which is the main government bank that controls the money supply and interest rates. It announced an overnight Variable Rate Repo auction for November 26, 2026. This auction has a notified amount of ₹75,000 crore and a tenor of 1 day.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India announced an overnight Variable Rate Repo auction for November 26, 2026, to manage near-term liquidity conditions. The auction carries a notified amount of ₹75,000 crore with a 1-day tenor under the liquidity adjustment facility.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India scheduled an overnight Variable Rate Repo auction for November 26, 2026, targeting ₹75,000 crore to address evolving liquidity conditions. The 1-day operation executes under the liquidity adjustment facility with a reversal date of November 27, 2026.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras payouts and crude exports, plus currency moves

stories.t: Petrobras Approves Payouts and Diverts Crude to Asia
stories.src: CPG Click Oil and Gas · The Globe and Mail
stories.b: Petrobras is a big oil company owned mostly by the Brazilian government. It approved a special payout of R$15.60bn for its investors. This kind of payout is an extra sum of money given to shareholders outside the normal schedule. At the same time, the company sent about 950,000 barrels of oil from its Libra field to Idemitsu in Japan. This is the first time it has shipped crude to Japan from this specific area. The shipment happened because supply problems in the Middle East caused by the Hormuz crisis forced buyers to look elsewhere.
stories.i: Petrobras approved an extraordinary payout of R$15.60bn for investors. The state-controlled energy firm also redirected roughly 950,000 barrels of pre-salt crude from its Libra field to Idemitsu in Japan. This marks the company's first-ever crude delivery to Japan from the pre-salt layer. The transaction took place as supply constraints in the Middle East stemming from the Hormuz crisis disrupted normal trade routes.
stories.a: Petrobras sanctioned an extraordinary remuneration totaling R$15.60bn for equity holders. Concurrently, the state-backed producer dispatched approximately 950,000 barrels of pre-salt crude from the Libra field to Idemitsu, constituting its maiden crude export to Japan. This geographical redirection materialized as the Hormuz crisis constricted Middle Eastern petroleum flows, compelling buyers to reconfigure supply chains.

stories.t: Brazilian Real Rises Against Major Currencies
stories.b: The US dollar fell around 1.5% against the Brazilian real. High interest rates, which are the cost of borrowing money, helped calm worries about the currency losing value. Euro and pound sterling rates also drifted lower against the real. Meanwhile, Planning and Budget Minister Moretti said the government should extend a diesel subsidy of BRL 2.12 for another 30 days.
stories.i: The US dollar dropped roughly 1.5% against the Brazilian real. Easing depreciation concerns stemmed from recent fiscal reforms and high domestic interest rates. The euro and pound sterling also edged lower against the real amid ongoing market indecision. Separately, Planning and Budget Minister Moretti stated that the government plans to extend the BRL 2.12 diesel subsidy for an additional 30 days.
stories.a: The US dollar depreciated by approximately 1.5% against the Brazilian real. Transmission channels for this currency strength include high domestic interest rates and recent fiscal reforms that curtailed capital flight fears. Concurrently, cross rates for the euro and pound sterling drifted lower against the real. In fiscal policy updates, Planning and Budget Minister Moretti announced that the administration intends to prolong the BRL 2.12 diesel subsidy for 30 days.

politics.b: Planning and Budget Minister Moretti stated that the government should extend the BRL 2.12 diesel subsidy for 30 days. Fiscal reforms and high interest rates eased concerns about the local currency losing value.
politics.i: Planning and Budget Minister Moretti indicated that the government should prolong the BRL 2.12 diesel subsidy for 30 days. Fiscal reforms and high borrowing costs helped stabilize the real against foreign currencies.
politics.a: Planning and Budget Minister Moretti confirmed plans to extend the BRL 2.12 diesel subsidy for a 30-day window. Concurrently, structural fiscal reforms and elevated monetary policy rates mitigated depreciation pressures on the real.

timeline: Planning and Budget Minister Moretti proposes a 30-day extension for the BRL 2.12 diesel subsidy.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: OPEC oil strategies, Aramco contracts, and regional conflict

stories.t: OPEC Oil Deal Extensions and Climate Talks Clash
stories.b: OPEC is a group of countries that work together to control how much oil they pump. This helps them manage the price of oil around the world. Saudi official Falih says the group needs to extend its current oil production deal. Meanwhile, the OPEC chief blames the European Union for the breakdown of the COP31 climate talks.
stories.i: OPEC officials confirm the absolute necessity of extending the current oil supply agreement. Saudi Arabia's Falih speaks on the matter while the broader organisation points fingers at the European Union for the COP31 climate collapse. Meanwhile, Kazakhstan and Iraq push the group for higher capacity ratings.
stories.a: OPEC representatives maintain the imperative for quota deal prolongations despite concurrent geopolitical friction. Saudi Arabia's Falih articulates the group consensus on supply management while leadership assigns blame to the European Union for COP31 breakdowns. Concurrently, Kazakhstan and Iraq lobby for elevated capacity baselines.

stories.t: Aramco Awards Contracts Amid Regional Security Pressures
stories.b: Aramco is the giant state-run oil company owned by Saudi Arabia. It just gave big engineering contracts to a company named Saipem for work on offshore oil fields. Yemen's Houthis are vowing to attack more Saudi airports and oil facilities after an earlier strike hit Aramco headquarters.
stories.i: Aramco issues multiple engineering, procurement, construction and installation contracts to Saipem for offshore fields in Saudi Arabia. The development unfolds as Yemen's Houthis pledge further attacks on Saudi airports and oil infrastructure following a strike on Aramco headquarters.
stories.a: Aramco distributes engineering, procurement, construction and installation awards to Saipem across multiple offshore assets. Operational security remains strained as Yemen's Houthis articulate targets on Saudi domestic airports and energy facilities subsequent to the Aramco headquarters strike.

politics.b: Saudi leaders manage state energy giant Aramco while dealing with foreign conflicts and international climate meetings.
politics.i: State policy balances oil quota diplomacy within OPEC against domestic infrastructure defense from regional drone and missile threats.
politics.a: State apparatuses navigate simultaneous OPEC supply adjustments, energy sector capital expenditure via Aramco, and direct physical security risks from regional actors.

timeline: OPEC officials debate production quotas and capacity ratings while blaming the European Union for climate talks collapse.
Aramco awards new offshore engineering contracts to Saipem following recent attacks near its headquarters.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Stock selloff and currency moves in Nigeria

stories.t: Nigerian Stocks Drop as Market Loses Value
stories.b: Share prices on the Nigerian stock exchange fell by 0.69%. This drop wiped 1.10 trillion naira off the total value of companies listed on the exchange. A share is a small piece of a company that people can buy and sell. When the main index falls, it means many of those company values went down at the same time.
stories.i: The main index of the Nigerian Exchange fell by 0.69% during a mid-week selloff. This decline erased 1.10 trillion naira in corporate market capitalization. Such sessions reflect broader liquidations across domestic equities.
stories.a: The NGXASI contracted by 0.69%, resulting in a 1.10 trillion naira vaporization of market capitalization amid broad-based institutional and retail liquidations. This compression highlights ongoing duration and equity risk premium adjustments within local portfolios.

stories.t: Central Bank Adjusts Dollar Limits as Currency Fluctuates
stories.b: The Central Bank of Nigeria raised the weekly dollar limit for bureau de change operators to 1,000,000 dollars. Bureau de change operators are licensed shops where people can exchange one country's money for another. Officials made this change to ease pressure on the naira, which is the currency of Nigeria. Meanwhile, the naira traded at 1,460 to the dollar at bureau de change windows.
stories.i: The Central Bank of Nigeria lifted the weekly dollar allocation limit for bureau de change operators to $1m to alleviate pressure on the naira. Interbank foreign exchange turnover surged 328% to reach $703m. At bureau de change windows, the naira weakened to 1,460 per US dollar.
stories.a: The Central Bank of Nigeria expanded the weekly foreign exchange threshold for bureau de change operators to $1m to relieve structural friction on the naira. Interbank trading volumes expanded 328% to $703m, concurrent with spot rates adjusting to 1,460 per US dollar in parallel segments.

politics.b: Political campaigns in Nigeria are underway. The Kogi State government paid 25,000,000 naira for 2027 campaign signage. In Zamfara State, authorities allocated 1.47 billion naira to buy arms for residents to defend themselves against bandits.
politics.i: Nigeria's political campaigns intensified alongside currency fluctuations and reserve movements. The Kogi State government paid 25,000,000 naira for 2027 campaign signage. In Zamfara State, the government allocated 1.47 billion naira to provide weapons for residents.
politics.a: Fiscal outlays accelerated as political campaigns commenced nationwide, exerting simultaneous pressure on foreign reserves and exchange rate stability. The Kogi State government disbursed 25,000,000 naira for 2027 campaign signage. Separately, the Zamfara State administration committed 1.47 billion naira to procure local security arms.

timeline: Interbank FX turnover reached $703m while the NGXASI fell 0.69%

Australia.label: Australia
Australia.sub: Metal selloffs outweigh hot inflation data for the dollar

stories.t: Currency Pressures From Commodity Declines
stories.b: The Australian dollar faced downward pressure because commodity prices fell. Commodities are raw materials like metals that countries buy and sell in bulk. This drop outweighed recent hot consumer price index readings. The consumer price index is a measure of how fast the prices of everyday goods are rising.
stories.i: The Australian currency declined as a widespread metal selloff overshadowed strong inflation figures. Brown Brothers Harriman noted that the downward pull from falling commodity values exceeded the support usually provided by elevated price growth measures. Traders adjusted positions as industrial materials faced heavy selling across global exchanges.
stories.a: Brokers at Brown Brothers Harriman highlighted that depreciating base metals exerted a stronger downward vector on the Australian dollar than the upside impetus from firm consumer price index prints. Price action demonstrates that currency desks are currently weighting raw material demand indices more heavily than domestic pricing pressures. This dynamic reveals heightened sensitivity to external commodity cycles over domestic monetary policy inputs.

stories.t: Corporate Updates Across Mining and Biotech
stories.b: Empire Metals lodged a prospectus with regulators for share trading. Vectus Biosystems updated investors on feedback for its lung fibrosis drug candidate from regulators. Saferoads Holdings spoke to shareholders about trailer sales and tariffs at its annual meeting.
stories.i: Empire Metals filed its prospectus with ASIC and the ASX. Vectus Biosystems processed pre-IND feedback from the FDA regarding its experimental lung fibrosis treatment. Saferoads Holdings briefed shareholders at its annual general meeting on ORG product sales and United States tariffs.
stories.a: Empire Metals advanced its market positioning by lodging an official prospectus with ASIC and the ASX. Vectus Biosystems evaluated FDA pre-IND guidance for its proprietary pulmonary fibrosis candidate, while Saferoads Holdings addressed US tariff exposure and Chameleon trailer operations during its annual general meeting.

politics.b: No political updates were reported for Australia today.
politics.i: No political developments or policy announcements were released.
politics.a: No macroeconomic policy shifts or legislative updates were registered in the session data.
